questions.question: What does sample_uniform(num_frames_total=5, T=8) return after the available frames are exhausted?
options: Eight new frames with indices 0 through 7
Only the first frame repeated eight times
Indices 0 through 4 followed by three copies of index 4
A random permutation of all five frames
questions.explanation: The function returns every available index and pads the sequence with the last frame until it has length T.

questions.question: What input shape does FramePool expect for a batch of two clips with eight RGB frames of size 64x64?
questions.explanation: FramePool reads N,T from the first two dimensions, flattens them through the 2D backbone, then averages T frame features.

questions.question: What output shape does FramePool return for that batch with num_classes=10?
questions.explanation: Temporal mean pooling produces one 512-dimensional vector per clip, and the head maps each vector to ten logits.

questions.question: How does inflate_2d_to_3d initialize a 3D kernel from a 2D kernel?
options: Copies only the first spatial row and zeros all other slices
Repeats the 2D weights across the time kernel and divides by the time size
Averages the input frames before applying the 2D convolution
questions.explanation: The code unsqueezes the 2D weights, repeats them time_kernel times, and divides by time_kernel to preserve the response scale.

questions.question: What factorisation does Conv2Plus1D implement?
options: A temporal-only convolution followed by image resizing
Two independent 2D convolutions with no time axis
A spatial 1xKxK convolution followed by a temporal Kx1x1 convolution
A linear classifier followed by frame sampling
questions.explanation: The spatial Conv3d mixes height and width first; BatchNorm/ReLU intervene before the temporal Conv3d mixes frames.

questions.question: What information can a 2D backbone plus FramePool miss compared with a true temporal model?
options: The RGB channels of every frame
The spatial features within each individual frame
The order and motion pattern of frames, because it averages frame features
questions.explanation: Mean pooling retains an aggregate appearance signal but cannot distinguish sequences with the same frames in different temporal orders.
